newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU still has problems with Kesko deal - EU source.
newsitem.headline: EU still has problems with Kesko deal - EU source.

text.p: The European Commission still has problems with the planned merger between Finnish wholesaler and retailer Kesko and its rival Tuko, European Union sources said on Wednesday.
They said a Kesko proposal last week to sell its TukoSpar Oy unit in 1997 to gain European Union approval of the merger would not be a sufficient remedy.
"We have nothing new to say," said Kesko spokesman Erkki Heikkinen, but he added that he was not aware of any new problems in the EU with Kesko's proposals.
One EU source said Kesko must come up with a new proposal quickly, "otherwise it is going to be complicated."
The deadline for a Commission decision whether to clear or block the merger is on November 26.
"We had and we have problems with it," one source said.
The Commission's approach to the case won approval from the EU's advisory committee on mergers when it met on Tuesday.
One committee source said Kesko/Tuko would have to come up with something more, "otherwise there is going to be no surprise that the (Commission's) decision will not be favourable."
EU sources said Kesko's proposal on October 28 to sell TukoSpar in 1997 had been tested on the market place and had not proven to be a "suitable remedy."

Kesko said at the time the proposal was in response to the Commission's preliminary ruling in mid-September that the merger between wholesale and retail groups Kesko and Tuko could be against EU merger rules.

Under the proposal, TukoSpar Oy would be formed into a separate wholesale and retail unit and sold to outsiders, while Tuko would retain control of its Spar merchant group operations as well as retail chains Anttila Oy and Rautia Oy.

The unit to be formed and sold would have net sales from wholesale operations worth 4.5 billion markka which is equal to about 40 percent of Tuko's 1995 net sales, Kesko said. -- Fredrik Dahl, +32 2 287 68 11
